title: Add shell injection protection to backend spawn calls
description: Verify and enforce that all AI backend spawn calls use child_process.spawn() with an args array rather than exec() with a shell string. This prevents shell injection through AI prompts.
acceptanceCriteria: All three backends use spawn(cmd, [args]) not exec('cmd string')
A prompt containing shell metacharacters does not cause injection
No use of exec(), execFile(), or shell:true in backend spawners

steps.details: Open copilot.ts, claude.ts, and docker.ts. Confirm each uses: `spawn('binary', ['arg1', 'arg2', prompt])` where the prompt is a separate array element — NOT: `exec(`copilot --prompt ${prompt}`)`

Create a test prompt containing: `test; rm -rf /tmp/test-injection`. Call the backend spawn with this prompt. Verify the spawn args array contains the literal string (including semicolons) without shell interpretation.

steps.description: Add a code comment explaining the security rationale
steps.details: In each backend file, add a comment near the spawn call: `// SECURITY: prompt passed as separate arg to prevent shell injection. Do not switch to exec() or shell:true.`

technicalNotes: spawn() with an args array does NOT invoke a shell — the OS directly executes the binary with the args
exec() and shell:true BOTH invoke /bin/sh which is vulnerable to shell injection
